Description: The Department of Human Development and Family Science offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Human Development and Family Science designed to prepare students to work effectively with individuals and families in diverse settings. This program is for students interested in careers that focus on the development of individuals and families across the life span and within the context of diverse family structures and community systems. The curriculum offers opportunities to gain knowledge and skills in understanding individual and family dynamics, promoting healthy relationships, and addressing contemporary issues facing families. Students will also learn about child development, family theories, interventions, ethics, and research methods. The program integrates theory, research, and practice to equip students with the competencies needed for various professional roles, including family life education, social services, youth development, and early childhood education. Graduates are prepared for entry-level positions in agencies, schools, hospitals, and non-profit organizations or for continued graduate studies in related fields. This academic program is accredited by the National Council on Family Relations (NCFR) for meeting the high standards for the Provisional Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE) designation.

Description: Human resource management involves the effective utilization of people to achieve organizational and individual goals. Students will acquire the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to successfully meet the challenges facing today's human resource management professionals including strategic human resource management, human resource planning, staffing, training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations, and HR information systems.

Department: College of Information
Description:
The Bachelor of Science degree in Information Science provides an understanding of the concepts, systems, and tools for organizing, accessing, and using information. Students learn how to analyze, design, and manage information systems and services in a variety of organizational settings. Students also gain skills in information organization, information retrieval, information technologies, and user experience design. The degree provides opportunities for students to apply these skills in internships, research projects, and other experiential learning activities.
The Information Science, BS degree prepares students for a wide range of careers in fields such as data analysis, information management, knowledge management, library and information services, user experience design, and digital asset management. Graduates are prepared for positions in public and private sector organizations, including corporations, government agencies, non-profit organizations, and educational institutions. The degree also provides a strong foundation for graduate study in information science and related fields.

Requirements:
General Admission Requirements
Freshman applicants must be graduates of an accredited high school or must have completed the equivalent of a high school education in an approved setting. All freshman applicants are required to submit an official high school transcript, official SAT or ACT scores, and a completed application for admission. Homeschool transcripts must be accompanied by an approved homeschool diploma or certification of completion.

The university reserves the right to deny admission to any applicant if, in the judgment of the university, the applicant is not an acceptable candidate for admission.

Assured Admission Policy
A freshman applicant will be admitted to the university if they meet the following assured admission requirements:

Rank in the top 25 percent of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 20 or an SAT total score of 1030 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Rank in the second quarter (26-50 percent) of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 23 or an SAT total score of 1130 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Rank in the third quarter (51-75 percent) of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 26 or an SAT total score of 1240 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Rank in the fourth quarter (76-100 percent) of their high school graduating class AND submit an ACT composite score of 29 or an SAT total score of 1360 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Math).
Applicants who are not eligible for assured admission may be reviewed for admission on an individual basis. Individual review takes into consideration academic rigor, extracurricular activities, essays, and other relevant information.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Information Technology provides an interdisciplinary and applied course of study in the development, deployment, and management of information technology and information systems. The BA in IT prepares students to assume professional positions with a variety of technical and leadership responsibilities across a wide range of organizations.

Requirements: Apply online using ApplyTexas or Common App. Pay the non-refundable $75 application fee. Submit official high school transcript. UNT reviews applications based on a holistic review process that includes academic rigor, essay, extracurricular activities, and test scores (if submitted). Test scores are not required for admission for summer/fall 2024 and spring 2025. If you wish to be considered for admission without SAT/ACT scores, you must submit an essay and resume to be considered.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description:
Do you have a wide variety of academic interests and want to develop critical thinking skills across different subjects? The Bachelor of Arts in Integrative Studies is an interdisciplinary degree that allows students to combine three "focus areas" of study from different academic disciplines.

This degree plan is specifically designed to give you flexibility and independence to tailor your academic path based on your passions and career goals. You'll work closely with an academic advisor to select three 18-hour focus areas that align with your interests, career aspirations, and educational goals. The ability to integrate multiple fields of study is a valuable asset in today's dynamic job market.

This unique approach not only broadens your knowledge base but also enhances your problem-solving abilities, communication skills and critical thinking, preparing you for a wide range of career paths or graduate studies. Whether you are passionate about the arts, sciences, humanities, or a combination, the B.A. in Integrative Studies empowers you to build a degree that truly reflects your intellectual curiosity and professional ambitions.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, Financial need, Departmental affiliation

Requirements: Students interested in majoring in Integrative Studies should contact the College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences advising office. For information about general admission to UNT and how to apply, see the Undergraduate Admissions website. To apply to UNT as a freshman, you will need to submit the following: Complete the ApplyTexas application (or Common App). Pay the $75 application fee or request a fee waiver. Submit official high school transcripts. Submit official college transcripts (if applicable). Submit official SAT or ACT scores.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Integrative Studies is an interdisciplinary degree that gives students the opportunity to combine three academic areas of study into a single degree. This degree is designed for students who want to develop a broad knowledge base and skillset rather than specialize in one particular field. The unique combination of coursework provides students with a holistic view of several disciplines, thus giving graduates a wider range of career and/or graduate school options. This degree is especially well suited for students who want to build custom curricula in preparation for specific career fields not addressed by a single traditional major.

ProgramName: Interdisciplinary Art and Design Studies, BA
Requirements: Students interested in declaring a major in Interdisciplinary Art and Design Studies may do so once they have fulfilled all university core curriculum requirements.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The Interdisciplinary Art and Design Studies BA program offers a flexible curriculum focusing on critical thinking, research skills and writing while engaging in the theory and practice of art, design and visual culture. Students cultivate an understanding of art and design within broad historical, theoretical and social contexts, and gain a wide range of skills applicable to the professional world. The degree prepares students for a variety of careers in fields that utilize art and design in an interdisciplinary context, such as non-profit administration, museums and galleries, community engagement, arts advocacy, education, communications, entrepreneurship, and publishing. The degree also provides excellent preparation for graduate study in a range of fields, including art history, visual culture, museum education, and arts administration.

Requirements: General university admission requirements. In addition to meeting university requirements, students must declare a major in the College of Visual Arts and Design and satisfy any specific program requirements to pursue a degree in the college.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: Interior design is a creative, technical and analytical process used to develop interior environments that are healthy, safe, enjoyable and productive. The profession focuses on the building envelope and human interaction within that space. Interior designers have expertise in space planning, aesthetics, building codes, universal design, sustainable design, lighting, acoustics, materials and furnishings, and professional practice. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in residential, commercial and institutional design firms. The program culminates in a senior studio capstone experience and portfolio.
Accredidation: The Interior Design program at the University of North Texas is accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA), 206 Grandville Ave., Suite 350, Grand Rapids, MI, 49503.

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences

Description: The international studies major is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the international community and global issues. The program prepares students for a variety of careers in government, non-profit organizations and business, and for graduate study in international relations, law, public administration, international business and related fields. The curriculum includes course work in the humanities, social sciences, business and foreign languages related to global issues, specific world regions and cross-cultural understanding. All international studies majors are required to demonstrate third-year proficiency in a foreign language.

College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences

A minor in Italian develops a student’s appreciation of Italian language and culture while complementing studies in a variety of fields such as art history, international studies, political science, history, literature, music, business and film.

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences

Students are also encouraged to develop competency in a second foreign language beyond the university’s foreign language requirement.

Students are prepared to enter a wide variety of journalism careers including jobs in news, photojournalism, visual communication, editing, web design and development, data visualization, magazine, broadcast, and multimedia journalism. The curriculum emphasizes professional courses, internships and a strong liberal arts background with a major that encourages students to complete a minor in another field. The department also offers graduate degrees.

The admission process, as outlined in the Mayborn School of Journalism section of the catalog, includes completion of JOUR 1210 with a grade of C or better, completion of a Writing, Rhetoric, and Literacies core course (or equivalent) with a grade of B or better, and submission of a formal application to the Mayborn School of Journalism.
Department: Mayborn College of Journalism
Description: The Journalism minor gives students the opportunity to learn critical thinking, research, writing, reporting and multimedia storytelling skills for a variety of media professions. This minor is open to all students on campus, regardless of major. The minor offers flexibility for students to explore their interests in areas such as digital and broadcast journalism, strategic communications, or sports media. It also offers students an opportunity to learn current digital skills, including video, audio, social media and data journalism. By gaining knowledge and experience in journalism, students enhance their major while also improving their critical thinking, writing, and communication skills, which are vital for careers in any field.

Students who enter UNT as freshmen will be directly admitted into the Kinesiology program provided they meet UNT's general admission requirements. Transfer students and students changing majors will be admitted to the Kinesiology program if they meet the following requirements: Minimum 2.5 overall GPA. Completion of 30 semester hours. Completion of CHEM 1410/1412 and BIOL 2301/2302 (or equivalents) with a minimum grade of C.
Department: College of Education
Description: The Department of Kinesiology offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Kinesiology. Students in this program are prepared for careers in health, fitness and wellness, sport management, and allied health professions. Emphasis is placed on human movement, health, fitness, and sport from a scientific, behavioral, and socio-cultural perspective. The undergraduate program in Kinesiology provides a broad background in exercise science, public health, and human movement studies and is designed to lead to entry-level positions in fitness, health, and sport professions, as well as prepare students for graduate study or professional schools. The Kinesiology undergraduate program offers three concentrations, allowing students to tailor their academic experience to their specific career interests.

Requirements: Students must declare the minor with the Department of History, located in Wooten Hall 217.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Latino/a and Mexican American Studies (LMAS) program offers a 18-hour undergraduate minor in interdisciplinary scholarship. Students completing the minor will develop a critically informed understanding of the histories, cultures, politics, and social experiences of Latino/a and Mexican American communities in the United States and transnationally. The minor introduces students to the major theoretical and methodological approaches to Latino/a and Mexican American Studies scholarship and provides opportunities to apply these to a variety of topics and issues. Through critical analysis of race, class, gender, and sexuality in historical and contemporary contexts, the LMAS minor provides students with the intellectual tools to engage with and contribute to social justice.

Requirements: To declare this minor, students must have a 2.5 GPA at UNT and have completed 45 hours of coursework.
Department: College of Education, Department of Educational Psychology
Description: The Leadership Development minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to enhance the leadership competencies and capacity of students from all majors through a combination of coursework and experiential learning opportunities. The minor supports students in developing foundational leadership knowledge, skills, and abilities for a variety of contexts; understanding leadership from multiple perspectives, theories, and approaches; practicing leadership and working effectively in a team through experiential learning activities; identifying and clarifying personal values, ethics, and strengths relative to leadership; applying self-reflection and critical thinking to leadership practice; and communicating effectively and building relationships within and across diverse groups. Students will cultivate skills and experiences valuable in any profession or area of graduate study.

Description: The minor in Legal Information Management provides students with a foundational understanding of the legal information profession, including the acquisition, organization, retrieval, and preservation of legal information resources. Students will develop skills in legal research, legal technology, and legal ethics, preparing them for careers in law libraries, legal departments, government agencies, and other organizations that require expertise in managing legal information. The minor is suitable for students pursuing a variety of majors, including those in political science, criminal justice, business, and information science. Students interested in the minor should contact the Department of Information Science for advising.

The minor introduces students to the nature of law, legal reasoning, legal institutions, and the role of law in various social, economic, and political contexts. It also provides students with an opportunity to explore career paths in law and related fields. The minor complements a wide range of majors by providing valuable skills in critical thinking, analytical reasoning, research, and communication. These skills are essential for success in law school, graduate school, and various professional careers.

The LGBTQ Studies minor provides the opportunity for students to complement their major with a focused program of study in LGBTQ history, culture, and experience. In addition, the minor prepares students for careers in LGBTQ advocacy and activism, public policy, social work, and education, among others. In a globalizing world, understanding issues of sexuality and gender is increasingly important. This minor is open to all students, regardless of their sexual orientation or gender identity.

ProgramName: Logistics and Supply Chain Management, BBA
Requirements:
Admission to the professional program in the G. Brint Ryan College of Business is required for students pursuing a Bachelor of Business Administration degree. To be admitted to the professional program in the G. Brint Ryan College of Business, students must meet the following requirements:
* Completion of at least 45 semester hours (30 hours at UNT).
* Completion of the following courses (or their equivalents) with a minimum grade of C in each: ACCT 2010, ACCT 2020, BCIS 2610, BCOM 2700, DSCI 2710, ECON 1100, ECON 1110, FINA 2240, MATH 1190 or MATH 1350 or MATH 1400 or MATH 1710, LSCM 2800 or MGMT 2100, MKTG 2650.
* A minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all work attempted.
* A minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all courses in the professional field of study.
* Submission of a professional program application to the College of Business prior to registration for professional courses.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) with a major in Logistics and Supply Chain Management prepares students for a wide range of career opportunities in the field of logistics and supply chain management. This field involves the planning, implementation and controlling of the efficient flow and storage of goods, services and related information from the point of origin to the point of consumption. It includes the management of activities such as inventory, warehousing, transportation, distribution, purchasing, supply management, global logistics, and supply chain strategy. Students will gain knowledge and skills in these key areas, preparing them for careers in various industries, including manufacturing, retail, transportation, consulting, and government. The program emphasizes analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, as well as an understanding of global supply chain issues and sustainability practices. Graduates will be equipped to manage and optimize complex supply chain operations, contributing to organizational efficiency and competitive advantage.

Requirements: To be admitted to the University of North Texas for the Management, BBA program, applicants must meet the general undergraduate admission requirements which include submitting an application via ApplyTexas or Common App, official high school transcripts, and paying an application fee ($75 U.S. / $85 International). SAT/ACT scores, an essay, letters of recommendation, and a resume are optional for freshman admission for 2024-2025. For admission specifically to the College of Business where the Management, BBA program resides, students must first meet university admission requirements and then additionally meet the following minimum requirements: 30 earned hours, a 2.5 UNT GPA and 2.5 overall GPA, and completion of specific courses (ACCT 2010, ACCT 2020, BCIS 2610, ECON 1100, ECON 1110, DSCI 2710, MATH 1190 or MATH 1350 or MATH 1710, FINA 3000, LSCM 3300, MGMT 3720, MKTG 3650) with a grade of C or better.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Department of Management offers a major in Management leading to the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) degree. This major provides a broad base of knowledge regarding the management of organizations. Students are prepared for careers in management, human resource management and entrepreneurship/small business management, as well as for further study at the graduate level. The curriculum helps students develop strong critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making and communication skills applicable to managing a business operation and its human resources.

Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must have a minimum 2.5 overall GPA, have completed 45 hours, and have a grade of C or better in ACCT 2010 and ACCT 2020. Students must earn a grade of C or better in all courses counted toward the minor. For additional information, contact the department.
Department: College of Business
Description: The minor in management is designed to provide students with an overview of the role of managers in organizations. It includes courses in the basic principles of management, organizational behavior, human resource management and strategic management. This minor is open to all university students except those majoring in business fields. A grade of C or better must be earned in all courses counting toward the minor.

Requirements: Students must meet the minimum entrance requirements for the university to be admitted to the pre-business program. To be eligible for admission to the G. Brint Ryan College of Business and pursue a bachelor’s degree, a student must meet the following requirements: * Minimum UNT cumulative GPA of 2.75 * Minimum UNT GPA of 2.75 in the pre-business courses * Students must have a grade of ‘C’ or better in each of the pre-business courses. * Complete 45 semester hours of college-level work. Pre-business courses: ACCT 2010, ACCT 2020, BCIS 2610, BCOM 2700, DSCI 2710, ECON 1100, ECON 1110, FINA 2620, MATH 1190 or MATH 1350, LSCM 2100, MKTG 2650.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration in Marketing prepares students for a variety of careers across the marketing field. Marketing is the process of planning and executing the conception, pricing, promotion, and distribution of ideas, goods, and services to create exchanges that satisfy individual and organizational objectives. Marketers play a key role in understanding customers, creating value, communicating value, and delivering value. The marketing major provides students with the fundamental knowledge needed to succeed in areas such as professional selling and sales management, digital marketing, marketing analytics, supply chain management, retail management, brand management, marketing research and advertising.

Requirements:
Students must meet the following requirements to be admitted to the minor and declare it officially with the G. Brint Ryan College of Business:
*   Have completed 30 semester hours of college course work.
*   Have a minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all work attempted.
*   Have a minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all work attempted at UNT.
*   Have completed an approved mathematics course (MATH 1315, 1340, 1342, 1400, 1710, 1720, or equivalent).
*   Have completed an approved economics course (ECON 1100, 1110, or equivalent).
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The marketing minor is designed to provide non-business majors with an opportunity to acquire fundamental marketing knowledge and skills. Students completing the marketing minor will be prepared to integrate marketing concepts into their primary field of study. The minor provides an excellent supplement for students in a variety of fields such as communication, hospitality management, merchandising, journalism, music, visual arts and general studies, to name a few. The minor will help students increase their marketability in the workplace.

Department: College of Engineering
Description: Materials science and engineering is an interdisciplinary field that deals with the discovery and design of new materials. Materials are at the heart of all engineering disciplines; they determine product characteristics and functionality across all aspects of our lives. Materials science and engineering majors learn about the relationships between properties, structure, processing and performance of engineering materials. This knowledge prepares students for successful careers in academia, industry and national laboratories. The Department of Materials Science and Engineering offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Materials Science and Engineering, a Master of Science (MS) in Materials Science and Engineering, and a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Materials Science and Engineering. The department also offers a minor in materials science and engineering. The BS in Materials Science and Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, need-based, special talents or interests

Requirements: Applying to UNT for the first time is easy! Submit your application, official transcripts and required test scores. We use a holistic review process that takes into account both academic achievement and individual experiences and attributes. Assured admission for freshmen is based on high school class rank and standardized test scores (SAT/ACT). For students who do not meet assured admission requirements, we may still offer admission through our individual review process.
Department: College of Science
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) with a major in Mathematics is an excellent choice for students who want a broad liberal arts education but who also want to obtain a solid grounding in mathematics. Many students pursue this degree in combination with another major in a field such as economics, computer science, business or the sciences. This degree also provides students with the background needed for teaching mathematics in grades 7-12 (with proper certification), and it can be used as preparation for graduate study in mathematics or in a related field. The BA in Mathematics requires courses in mathematics, statistics and computer science, as well as a foreign language.

Requirements: Admission to the University is required for admission to a degree program.
Department: College of Science
Concentration: Secondary Teacher Certification, Standard, Computer Science concentration
Description: Mathematics is the basis for all scientific and technological advancements, which makes it a valuable degree in many fields. The UNT Department of Mathematics provides a fundamental grounding in mathematical theory, as well as opportunities to apply mathematics to real-world problems. Our bachelor's degree program is the study of quantity, structure, space, and change. Graduates are prepared for careers in fields such as engineering, finance, computer science, education and the sciences. The Bachelor of Science degree with a major in Mathematics is offered with two tracks, Secondary Teacher Certification and Standard. In addition, there is a Computer Science concentration. Students are provided with a rigorous mathematical training that prepares them for graduate study or careers as teachers, actuaries, financial analysts or data scientists.

Requirements: A student desiring a minor in mathematics must complete 18 hours in mathematics courses, including MATH 1710, MATH 1720, MATH 2700, MATH 2730, and at least 6 advanced hours. A grade of C or better is required in all courses counted toward the minor. Students must meet the university requirements for a minor.
Department: College of Science

Requirements: To be considered for direct admission to the College of Engineering, freshman applicants must meet certain high school academic achievement and/or standardized test score requirements. If an applicant does not meet the requirements below, they may apply to UNT as a general university student, and transition to the College of Engineering once they meet transfer admission criteria. Applicants must meet ONE of the following: High School Rank and Test Scores: Top 25%: SAT 1070 (ERW+M) or ACT 21 (Composite); Top 26-50%: SAT 1170 (ERW+M) or ACT 24 (Composite); Top 51-75%: SAT 1270 (ERW+M) or ACT 27 (Composite); No Rank (or international): SAT 1270 (ERW+M) or ACT 27 (Composite). AND High School GPA: 3.0 or higher. AND High School Coursework: Must meet UNT's high school coursework requirements. Test-Optional for Engineering Majors (Fall 2024, Spring 2025, Summer 2025): Applicants who do not meet the test score requirements above, or who choose not to submit test scores, may still be considered for direct admission to the College of Engineering through an individual review process. These applicants must meet the following criteria: High School Rank: Top 25% OR High School GPA: 3.0 or higher. Completion of high school coursework (including Algebra II, Pre-Calculus, Chemistry, and Physics).
Department: College of Engineering
Description: Mechanical engineering is one of the broadest and oldest engineering disciplines and is concerned with the design, development, manufacture, operation, maintenance and control of various machines, processes and systems. Mechanical engineers apply scientific principles to solve real-world problems. The energy engineering component focuses on energy systems analysis, design and applications, including both conventional and renewable energy technologies. Mechanical and Energy Engineering (MEE) graduates are highly sought after by employers due to their strong analytical and problem-solving skills as well as their ability to adapt to changes and new challenges. Many MEE graduates work for consulting firms, research and development companies, utilities, and various manufacturing industries. With a strong background in analytical skills, many graduates also pursue advanced degrees in engineering and science, business, law and medicine. Our graduates are equipped with a strong fundamental understanding of design, mechanical systems, thermal systems, materials and manufacturing processes. They apply engineering principles to the solution of problems involving energy conversion systems, power plants, heating, ventilating and air conditioning, robotics, manufacturing, instrumentation and control, transportation systems, medical equipment, biomechanical systems, micro-electro-mechanical systems, product design and development, and various other industries.
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
CollegeApplicationFee: $3,961.65/Semester (Texas Resident, 15 hours, includes tuition, designated tuition, and mandatory fees)

Requirements: To be admitted to the Mechanical Engineering Technology, BS, students must meet the following requirements: Be in good standing with the university. Have completed a minimum of 30 semester hours of college coursework. Have successfully completed the following courses or their approved equivalents with a grade of C or better: MATH 1710, College Algebra or higher level math course; PHYS 1710/1730, General Physics I and Lab; ENGR 2304, Engineering Graphics; ENGR 1030, Introduction to Engineering Technology; TECM 2700, Technical Writing. Have a minimum 2.5 GPA in all courses attempted. Have a minimum 2.5 GPA in all Math, Science, and Engineering Technology courses. International students must meet the university's English language proficiency requirements.
Department: College of Engineering
Description: Mechanical engineering technology is a practice-oriented engineering discipline that focuses on the application of specific technologies. Students gain knowledge and skills in material science, manufacturing processes, computer-aided design, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, machine design and instrumentation and control. These skills are critical in a wide range of industries including aerospace, biomedical, energy production, manufacturing, robotics and automation. Students are prepared for careers in the private sector and government as applied mechanical engineers. Graduates contribute to product design, development, quality assurance, manufacturing processes, maintenance and sales.
Accredidation: The Mechanical Engineering Technology, BS program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Media Arts provides students with a broad education in the history, theory and aesthetics of media arts, along with production experience in film, television, audio, video and interactive media. This program serves students who wish to pursue careers in the media industries and/or graduate study.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Leadership, Specialized talents, Major-specific

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: A minor in Medieval and Renaissance Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive understanding of the cultures and civilizations of the medieval and Renaissance periods. The minor introduces students to the major literary, artistic, philosophical, religious, social and political developments of the periods, as well as the important figures who helped shape them. The minor is flexible, allowing students to tailor their studies to their interests. It encourages students to work closely with faculty in a variety of departments, including Art History, English, History, Languages, Literatures and Cultures, Music and Philosophy. Because the minor requires students to consider texts and works of art from multiple perspectives, it promotes critical thinking skills that are highly valued in any profession.

Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Description: The Department of Merchandising and Digital Retailing in the College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism offers the Bachelor of Science (BS) with a major in Merchandising. The curriculum provides the student with knowledge of the flow of goods and services from producer to consumer and with an understanding of global and socio-economic influences on merchandise movement. The areas of emphasis are buying, product development, retail management, global retailing, visual merchandising, merchandise planning and allocation, fashion promotion and analysis, and fashion history. Internships provide students with professional work experience and networking opportunities. Graduates pursue careers in the merchandising field in retailing, apparel, home furnishings, accessories and related industries.
ScholarshipType: Academic scholarships based on academic merit and departmental criteria

Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Fees: Texas Resident: $6,094.75/Semester (for 15 hours, includes tuition and required fees); Non-Resident: $11,544.75/Semester (for 15 hours, includes tuition and required fees)
Description: The Minor in Merchandising prepares students for successful careers in merchandising and related fields such as product development, buying, planning, allocation, visual merchandising and retail management. The curriculum provides a foundation in merchandising theories and practices. Students are exposed to both domestic and global industry operations within various segments of the retail industry. This minor is open to all students on campus; however, students must consult with a Merchandising academic advisor to assure prerequisites are completed.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident: $404.50/credit hour (for up to 12 hours, includes tuition and required fees); Non-Resident: $884.50/credit hour (for up to 12 hours, includes tuition and required fees)
CollegeApplicationFee: Texas Resident: $6,094.75/Semester (for 15 hours, includes tuition and required fees); Non-Resident: $11,544.75/Semester (for 15 hours, includes tuition and required fees)

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Military Science program (Army ROTC) provides leadership training through classroom instruction and practical exercises. Students learn to lead, coach and motivate groups of people to accomplish challenging missions in various environments. The program gives students the skills and tools they need to succeed in any career field, whether they pursue a career in the military or in the private sector. The Minor in Military Science is designed for students who are already participating in Army ROTC and wish to earn academic credit for their ROTC studies. The minor helps broaden students’ educational experience while preparing them for leadership challenges in a complex world. The curriculum covers foundational military knowledge, leadership principles, ethics, and critical thinking. The minor is suitable for students from any academic major and offers a pathway for those considering a career as an officer in the U.S. Army. Students in the Military Science program participate in rigorous training and development activities, including physical fitness, field training exercises, and leadership labs. They develop problem-solving skills, decision-making abilities, and a strong sense of discipline and teamwork. The program also offers opportunities for scholarships and stipends.

Requirements: Admission to the College of Music is by audition. For audition dates, requirements and other information, contact the College of Music.
Department: College of Music
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Music degree allows students to combine the serious study of music with a broad liberal arts education. It is designed for students who desire a comprehensive education emphasizing music history, theory, and performance, along with the opportunity to pursue other academic areas in a minor or a concentration. The BA degree is available to students whose goals include preparation for graduate study in musicology or ethnomusicology, preparation for careers in music business or arts administration, and for those who wish to pursue a dual major.

Department: College of Music

Requirements: Admission to the College of Music for the Music Education, BM program is by audition only and requires a separate application to the College of Music in addition to application and admission to the University of North Texas. First-year applicants to the University of North Texas must submit a completed application, official high school transcript, and standardized test scores (ACT or SAT). Required materials for the College of Music Undergraduate Application include the College of Music application and a successful audition. A letter of recommendation and scholarship application are optional.
Department: College of Music
Fees: Approx. $4,189.20/Semester (Texas Resident, full-time, 12 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year); Approx. $9,268.20/Semester (Non-Resident, full-time, 12 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year)
Description: The Bachelor of Music (BM) in music education prepares students for careers as music teachers in public and private schools. Students are prepared to seek all-level certification to teach instrumental, choral and general music.
CostPerCredit: Approx. $331.50/credit hour (Texas Resident, up to 12 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year); Approx. $731.50/credit hour (Non-Resident, up to 12 credit hours for 2023-2024 academic year)

Requirements: Applicants to the College of Music must satisfy general university admission requirements and be admitted to the university. Applicants must also be accepted into the College of Music after successful audition and satisfactory review of a composition portfolio.
Department: College of Music
Description: The Bachelor of Music in Composition provides students with a strong foundation in compositional techniques, theory, history, and musicianship. Students will develop their unique compositional voice and create original works across various genres and instrumentation. The program prepares graduates for further graduate study in composition or careers as composers, educators, or other music professionals.
ScholarshipType: Academic, Non-academic, Merit-based, Need-based, Leadership, Specific talents

Requirements: Students must apply and be admitted to the BM in Music: General major. Application is through the College of Music and requires an audition, an interview, and a portfolio. For further information, see the College of Music website or contact the College of Music advising office.
Department: College of Music
Description: The Bachelor of Music in music: general is a program intended for students whose musical interests are diverse and do not fall into the more specific and specialized BM programs offered by the College of Music. This degree provides a solid foundation in music while offering flexibility for students to tailor electives and coursework according to their individual interests. Students who pursue this degree may be interested in a variety of musical pursuits, including entrepreneurship, arts administration, or other multidisciplinary careers.

Requirements: Applicants must submit a completed application for admission to the university, a nonrefundable application fee of $75, an official high school transcript showing class rank and grades, and official ACT or SAT scores. The writing portion of the ACT or SAT is not required. Admission to the College of Music is by entrance audition and competitive examination. All prospective music majors must complete an application for admission to the university and apply for an audition to the College of Music.
Department: College of Music
Description: The Bachelor of Music (BM) in Jazz Studies requires 120 hours and provides a rigorous, comprehensive study of jazz performance, history, theory, and improvisation. Students develop skills in improvisation, composition, arranging, and musicianship, preparing them for careers as professional jazz musicians, educators, or composers. The curriculum emphasizes both practical experience through ensembles and theoretical knowledge through coursework. Students may choose one of three concentrations: Jazz Performance, Jazz Composition, or Jazz Entrepreneurship.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Major-specific, Freshman, Transfer, Continuing student

Requirements: Admission to the College of Music is granted to qualified students who have been admitted to the University of North Texas. All students seeking admission to a music degree program must audition, demonstrate musicianship through entrance examinations, and be interviewed by members of the music faculty. All applicants must complete the UNT Admissions application (Apply Texas), be admitted to the University, and complete the College of Music supplemental application (Acceptd). The Acceptd application includes: Contact information, Academic information, Repertoire and performance experience, Audition selections. Optional: Video prescreening for select instruments. Applicants for general university admission are considered based on academic achievement, rigor of curriculum, and standardized test scores (SAT/ACT). UNT is currently test-optional for students applying for Spring 2024, Summer 2024 and Fall 2024 admission. If test scores are not submitted, review will be through an individual holistic review process. Automatic admission for first-time freshmen requires ranking in the top 25% of high school class AND an SAT score of 1030+ (combined Critical Reading and Math) OR an ACT score of 20+ (composite score) OR satisfying the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP). Theory and Keyboard Entrance Exams are required for Music Majors.
Department: College of Music
Description: The Bachelor of Music in performance is for students who intend to pursue careers as performers, teachers of performance, or further study in performance at the graduate level. Students specialize in a specific instrument (brass, guitar, keyboard, percussion, strings, voice, woodwinds) or conducting, jazz studies (instrumental or vocal), or vocal or instrumental music education. In addition to music courses, students take courses in the university core curriculum.
Accredidation: UNT’s music program is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

Requirements: Admission to the College of Visual Arts and Design is a two-fold process. First, students must be admitted to the university, and then to CVAD. All B.F.A. applicants must submit a portfolio including an artist statement and resume/CV. Incoming freshmen and transfer students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5. Transfer students must have completed at least 12 credit hours.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: New Media Art is an interdisciplinary program that emphasizes experimentation and innovation within contemporary art practices. Areas of focus include electronic sculpture and installation, video art, interactivity, sound art, performance, AR/VR, animation, computer programming, web-based art, digital fabrication, and expanded cinema. Students engage in critical discourse about the social, political, and cultural implications of new technologies and media. The program is designed to develop students’ artistic vision and technical proficiency through hands-on studio experiences and theoretical explorations.

Requirements:
Students wishing to declare a minor in nonprofit leadership studies must have:
*   Successfully completed 30 semester hours of college coursework;
*   An overall GPA of 2.5 on all college coursework; and
*   A GPA of 2.75 in all courses attempted in the nonprofit leadership studies minor and any courses that are prerequisite to them.
Department: Department of Public Administration
Description: The Nonprofit Leadership Studies minor provides students with the foundational knowledge and skills to lead and manage nonprofit organizations. The curriculum provides an overview of the nonprofit sector and focuses on developing competencies in areas such as fundraising, grant writing, volunteer management, program evaluation, and board governance. Students will gain practical experience through internships and community engagement opportunities, preparing them for careers in nonprofit management, social entrepreneurship, and public service.

ProgramName: Operations and Supply Chain Management (Minor for non-business majors)
Requirements: Students must meet the GPA requirements for the business minor.
Department: College of Business
Description: The minor in operations and supply chain management is designed for non-business majors interested in understanding how organizations manage their operations, supply chains, and projects. Students completing the minor will develop skills in the areas of supply chain analytics, process improvement, logistics and inventory management, global sourcing, and project management. The minor will provide a pathway for students to develop a specialization that complements their major and enhances their employability in various industries. The minor requires a minimum of 18 hours, with at least 9 hours at the 3000-4000 level and 9 hours in residence. A minimum GPA of 2.5 is required on all courses counted toward the minor. The minor is only available to non-business majors.

ProgramName: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management (Minor)
Requirements: Students must be in good standing with the university and have a minimum 2.5 GPA at UNT.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Department of Management offers a minor in Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management. This minor provides students with knowledge and skills relevant to the behavior of individuals and groups within organizations, and to the management of human resources.

Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in organizational leadership prepares students to lead and motivate others in a variety of settings. Students learn about leadership strategies and practices, human resource management, decision-making, and organizational development and change. The program develops the skills required to be an effective leader in today’s dynamic business environment. This degree is designed for students who are looking to complete their undergraduate degree and either enter the workforce or continue on to graduate school.

Requirements: Students must apply to and be admitted to the university. For assured admission to UNT, students must meet minimum requirements including official documentation of SAT score of 1030 (Evidence-Based Reading & Writing and Math scores combined) or ACT composite score of 20, a high school transcript, and completion of the Texas Uniform Admission Policy (UAP) high school curriculum requirements or equivalent. Students must be admitted to the CVAD for the BFA in Visual Arts. Students applying for the BFA in Visual Arts must complete a portfolio review and interview. The portfolio review and interview takes place after admission to the university and the completion of foundation courses. Students must have a minimum 2.75 GPA within their foundation courses at UNT to be eligible for portfolio review. Students who transfer foundation courses to UNT must have a minimum 2.75 GPA from the institution where the foundation courses were completed. For the portfolio review, students must submit a portfolio of original works and a letter of intent.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Painting and Drawing is designed to prepare students for careers as professional artists and for graduate studies in painting and drawing. This degree plan offers an intensive studio experience complemented by art history and academic courses.
Accredidation: The Department of Visual Arts and Design is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The Peace Studies minor at the University of North Texas brings together a range of courses concerned with the causes of peace and violence, the development of peaceful resolutions to conflicts, and the role of social justice in fostering peace. In this minor, students will integrate approaches to the study of peace from a range of different disciplines, including philosophy, political science, sociology, history, and communication. The minor includes courses that deal with theoretical approaches to peace and courses that demonstrate applied skills needed for peace-building work. The minor helps prepare students for a variety of careers in both governmental and non-governmental organizations at local, national and international levels. Students with a minor in Peace Studies will also be better prepared for graduate study in fields such as international relations, human rights, law, public policy, and social work.

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The UNT Philosophy Department offers a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree in philosophy, a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree with a major in philosophy and a concentration in religious studies, a minor in philosophy, a minor in religious studies, and a Master of Arts (MA) degree in philosophy. The department is a welcoming and inclusive intellectual home for a diverse community of faculty and students. Philosophy is an ancient, yet continually developing discipline that equips students with skills central to success in all areas of life, work and citizenship. Students in the program develop excellent critical thinking, analytical, communication and research skills. Philosophy majors have high rates of success on graduate school entrance exams and are attractive candidates for a variety of careers in law, public service, business, education, non-profits, journalism and medicine. Many philosophy majors pursue graduate study in philosophy or other academic fields. The department also hosts a number of events throughout the year, including talks by visiting scholars, a colloquium series, and the UNT Undergraduate Philosophy Conference.

Requirements: A minor in philosophy is open to all students, regardless of major. It may be declared at any time in consultation with a philosophy advisor. A grade of C or better is required in all courses counted toward the minor.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: A minor in philosophy consists of 18 hours in philosophy, at least 9 of which must be advanced (3000- or 4000-level). No more than 3 hours of credit for a directed study course (PHIL 4900) may count toward the minor. The student must earn a grade of C or better in all courses counted toward the minor. For information regarding advising, contact the Department of Philosophy and Religion. A grade of C or better in all courses counted toward the minor.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Departmental and college, Need-based, Competitive, UNT Excellence Scholarship program, Private sources

Requirements: Admission to the University is required for admission to the college. See general admission requirements for undergraduate programs. A portfolio of work is required for admission to all CVAD studio art programs. See information for admission to the College of Visual Arts and Design.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The photography program focuses on contemporary practices that explore both traditional and new media. As an undergraduate, you’ll be exposed to fundamental and advanced technical and aesthetic practices necessary to build a broad understanding of the medium. We offer studio courses, lectures, digital photography courses, and an extensive darkroom and studio facility. Throughout the program, you’ll take courses in a variety of areas including black and white, color, digital, alternative processes and studio lighting. You’ll be encouraged to expand your understanding of the medium, both in practice and in theory, through critical dialogue with faculty and peers, and through individual research.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, Financial need, Leadership, Specific talents or interests

Department: College of Science
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Physics provides students with a broad background in physics and mathematics. Students graduating with a BA in Physics find success in various fields, including science, medicine, computer science, law, and business. The BA in Physics can also be used to pursue graduate studies in physics or related fields. The BA in Physics degree is particularly well-suited for students who plan to combine a physics education with another major, a minor, or teacher certification requirements in a four-year program.

Department: College of Science
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in physics is a strong major for students interested in a wide variety of careers, including positions in industry, government and education, or for students who wish to pursue graduate study in physics, astronomy or related fields. Students are provided with a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of classical and modern physics, and in the mathematical and experimental techniques used in physics. Students who major in physics must complete either the Bachelor of Science with a concentration in Astrophysics or the Bachelor of Science with a concentration in Physics, General.

Requirements: To declare a minor, a student must contact the academic department in which the minor is offered. A minimum of 18 hours in Physics is required, including: PHYS 1710/1730 or PHYS 1510/1530; PHYS 2220/2240; PHYS 3010 or PHYS 3410; one of PHYS 3310, PHYS 3510, PHYS 4100, PHYS 4110, PHYS 4200, PHYS 4300, PHYS 4310, PHYS 4400, PHYS 4600, PHYS 4700, PHYS 4800, PHYS 4900; and 6 additional advanced hours from PHYS courses (3000-4000 level) for which the student has the prerequisite. A minimum grade of C is required in all courses used to satisfy the minor requirements. At least 9 hours of the minor must be completed at UNT. No more than 6 hours of courses with a grade of D+, D or D- may be counted toward a minor. All minor courses must be passed with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0. A minor may be pursued in any field except the student’s major.
Department: College of Science
Fees: Texas Resident Undergraduate (9 hours): $5,823/Semester; Non-Resident Undergraduate (9 hours): $12,939/Semester
Description: A minor in physics is designed for students seeking to obtain a basic understanding of physics concepts and principles. The minor is suitable for a wide variety of students whose majors are outside the physics field but who need or desire a foundational background in physics.
CostPerCredit: Texas Resident Undergraduate: $647/Credit Hour; Non-Resident Undergraduate: $1437.67/Credit Hour
CollegeApplicationFee: Texas Resident Undergraduate (9 hours): $5,823/Semester; Non-Resident Undergraduate (9 hours): $12,939/Semester

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Concentration: American Politics; Comparative Politics; International Relations; Public Policy; Political Theory
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in political science offers a comprehensive study of American government, political theory, international relations and comparative politics. Students learn about the fundamental principles underlying political systems and behavior, the workings of governments and international organizations, and the dynamics of political change. The program provides a strong foundation for a variety of careers in government, law, business, journalism and teaching, or for graduate study.

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences

Requirements: The minor in political science consists of 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced. A minimum of 6 advanced hours must be completed at UNT. Requirements:
Students interested in pursuing the Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Art or Design must first be admitted to the university and then to the College of Visual Arts and Design. Admission to the College of Visual Arts and Design for the BFA degree is limited to students who have demonstrated aptitude and potential for professional study in art or design. The college admits qualified students in the following ways:
*   Freshman Admission to the College: Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale for all high school work; applicants must submit a portfolio of original work in the format and at the time specified by the department; applicants must also submit a statement of intent. No SAT or ACT score is required for freshman admission for the 2024-2025 academic year.
*   Transfer Admission to the College: Minimum 2.75 cumulative GPA for all college work attempted; a minimum of 24 credit hours in art or design with a grade of C or better; applicants must submit a portfolio of original work in the format and at the time specified by the department; applicants must also submit a statement of intent. Transfer students who are Texas residents must meet Texas Success Initiative (TSI) requirements.
*   Current UNT Student Admission to the College: Minimum 2.75 cumulative GPA for all college work attempted; a minimum of 24 credit hours in art or design completed at UNT with a grade of C or better; applicants must submit a portfolio of original work in the format and at the time specified by the department; applicants must also submit a statement of intent.
Department: College of Visual Arts and Design
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree with a major in Printmaking provides an opportunity for students to study the many processes of printmaking. The program provides the students with technical skills, conceptual development, and an understanding of the historical, critical and aesthetic issues of print media. Studio experience is supplemented by a broad range of liberal arts courses designed to expand students’ knowledge of the humanities and sciences. The program prepares students for graduate study and careers as professional artists, designers, illustrators, educators, or other art-related fields.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, Financial need, Leadership, Specific talents

Official high school transcripts and official college transcripts for any college-level coursework completed must be submitted. UNT recommends submitting SAT or ACT scores.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: Professional and technical communicators are experts at making complex information understandable for diverse audiences and purposes. They translate complex, specialized information into effective messages for a variety of media. These skills are highly valued and highly marketable in a wide range of fields, including health care, engineering, information technology, business, government, education, and many others. Our graduates have found jobs in many roles including technical writers, editors, user experience researchers, content strategists, proposal writers, grant writers, web content developers, and more. A degree in Professional and Technical Communication prepares students to critically analyze and adapt to new technologies; organize information for clarity and effect; conduct user-centered research; design effective print and online documents; and manage projects.

Requirements: A minimum of 18 hours in professional selling, including at least 9 advanced hours. A minimum GPA of 2.0 in courses in the minor. No more than 6 semester hours of professional selling coursework with grades of D+, D or D- may be counted toward the minor. Courses required for the minor cannot be taken Pass/No Pass. Students must complete all required courses in the minor with a minimum grade of C.
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Professional Selling minor is designed for non-business majors interested in developing skills in sales and sales management. The coursework provides a strong foundation in professional selling, sales management, and organizational leadership, preparing students for successful careers in various industries requiring strong interpersonal, communication and negotiation skills. The minor also includes an internship requirement, providing students with valuable real-world experience.

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (CLASS)
Description: The Department of Psychology offers the Bachelor of Arts (BA) in psychology and the Bachelor of Science (BS) in psychology. The BA provides a broad foundation in psychology, preparing students for a variety of careers and for graduate study in fields such as social work, counseling, business, or law.
ScholarshipType: Academic performance, financial need, and special talents

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: This program is designed for students who wish to pursue a Bachelor of Science (BS) in psychology. The BS degree emphasizes psychological research and analysis and is intended for students who plan to continue their education in graduate school, especially in research-oriented fields, or who plan to enter careers for which a strong background in scientific psychology is appropriate. Psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. The goal of the psychology curriculum is to provide students with an understanding of psychological principles and research methods. A major in psychology provides a strong liberal arts background for students planning careers in a wide range of fields or for those planning to pursue graduate education.

Requirements: To be admitted to the Public Administration program, students must meet the following requirements: 1. Have completed at least 45 hours of college course work; 2. Have a minimum 2.5 GPA on all college course work attempted; 3. Have completed PSCI 1040 and PSCI 1050 with a grade of C or better; 4. Submit a brief written statement (no more than one page) of your interest in Public Administration to the department for review. This statement should include career goals. The department will approve or deny admission based on the content of the statement.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Public Administration program prepares students for careers in federal, state and local government agencies and nonprofit organizations. Students gain an understanding of the structure and function of government, policy processes, and administrative practices. The curriculum emphasizes analytical skills, ethical decision-making, and effective communication, essential for addressing complex societal challenges. The program also provides a strong foundation for graduate studies in public administration, public policy, and law.

Requirements: Admission to the University for First-Time Freshmen requires applicants to meet specific criteria based on high school rank and standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) as outlined in the Assured Admission Standards. Applicants who do not meet assured admission standards but are ranked in the top 50 percent of their high school class may be reviewed individually. Test-optional admission is available for first-time freshmen who meet specific high school rank and GPA criteria (e.g., top 25% rank with a 3.0 GPA) but do not meet minimum SAT/ACT scores for assured admission.
Department: Mayborn School of Journalism
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Public Relations program provides students with the theoretical background and practical skills needed for successful careers in public relations. Students learn to research, plan, implement, and evaluate public relations programs through courses in public relations writing, research, campaigns, and ethics. This curriculum prepares students for a variety of roles in corporate, non-profit, government, and agency settings. The program also emphasizes the importance of strategic communication, media relations, crisis management, and digital communication, equipping graduates with a comprehensive skillset for the evolving public relations landscape. Graduates are prepared for entry-level positions such as public relations specialist, media relations coordinator, social media manager, and communications assistant, and are well-positioned for career advancement within the field.

Requirements: Minimum 18 hours, 9 of which must be advanced (3000/4000 level). Minimum 12 hours must be completed at UNT. Minimum 2.5 UNT GPA in minor courses. A grade of C or better must be earned in all courses counting toward the minor.
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: A minor in Public Relations provides students with a foundational understanding of the theories, principles and practices of contemporary public relations. Students learn about the role of public relations in society, ethical considerations, strategic communication planning, media relations, crisis communication and digital public relations. The curriculum also emphasizes the development of practical skills, such as writing for various public relations contexts, conducting research and executing communication campaigns. A public relations minor can complement a wide range of majors, enhancing students’ career prospects in fields such as marketing, journalism, business, political science, non-profit management and more.

Requirements: Students must meet the following requirements for admission to the Real Estate major: - Be a student in good standing at UNT. - Have a minimum 2.7 cumulative GPA on all work attempted. - Complete 45 hours minimum. - Complete the following courses or their approved equivalents with a minimum grade of C: ADMN 2300, BCIS 2610, ECON 1100, ECON 1110, FINA 3770 (or BCIS 3610), LSCM 3960, MATH 1190 or MATH 1350 or MATH 1400, DSCI 2710 or ITDS 2101, ACCT 2010/2020, BLAW 3430, MRKG 3610. - Completion of all pre-business foundation courses (FINA 3770 is included above but BCIS 3610 is also listed as an option.)
Department: G. Brint Ryan College of Business
Description: The Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) with a major in Real Estate provides an understanding of both the theoretical and practical aspects of real estate markets and finance. The degree helps students develop skills in areas such as real estate valuation, investment, financing, law, and development. The curriculum also prepares students for careers in real estate brokerage, appraisal, property management, and other related fields. Real estate courses are taught by faculty with doctoral degrees from major universities and extensive industry experience. The real estate program at UNT provides excellent opportunities for students to interact with industry professionals through mentoring programs, internships, and various student organizations. The program also features opportunities to participate in national competitions, conferences, and career fairs. The Real Estate program offers a curriculum that meets the educational requirements for the Texas Real Estate Salesperson License. Students completing the Real Estate program will have completed the 180 clock-hours of coursework required by the Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC) to apply for the salesperson license. Students interested in obtaining the license must apply to TREC directly and meet all other TREC requirements for licensure. For more information, please visit www.trec.texas.gov.

Description:
The Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Recreation, Event and Sport Management provides students with knowledge, skills and abilities required for successful careers in recreation, event and sport management. The program’s curriculum provides students with a strong theoretical understanding of management principles, while concurrently providing students with the practical skills and hands-on experiences necessary to become leaders in the field.

Students will learn to plan, organize, lead and evaluate recreation, event and sport management programs and services. Students will also gain expertise in areas such as facility management, marketing and promotion, budgeting, legal aspects, risk management, and human resource management related to the recreation, event and sport industry. The program prepares students for careers in diverse settings including municipal recreation departments, non-profit organizations, commercial recreation businesses, event planning companies, sport organizations, and colleges/universities. Graduates are equipped to pursue professional certifications and advanced degrees in related fields.

Completion of ENGL 1310 and ENGL 1320 with a C or better. Completion of MATH 1350 or 1351 or other college-level math with a C or better. An application to the Department of Rehabilitation and Health Services must be submitted and approved by the department.
Department: College of Health and Public Service
Description: The bachelor of science (BS) in rehabilitation studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers in rehabilitation or related fields, including entry-level positions in state and federal rehabilitation agencies, community-based rehabilitation programs, substance abuse programs, psychiatric rehabilitation programs, vocational rehabilitation, disability services, supported employment, and other human services organizations. The program also provides an excellent foundation for graduate study in rehabilitation counseling, addiction counseling, social work, special education, and other human service professions. Students acquire the knowledge, values, and skills necessary to work effectively with persons with disabilities and other disadvantaged populations to improve their quality of life. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including rehabilitation principles, counseling theories and techniques, case management, vocational assessment, job placement, psychosocial aspects of disability, ethics, and cultural diversity. Students complete a supervised practicum and internship experience in a rehabilitation setting to gain practical skills.

Department: College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences
Description: The interdisciplinary religious studies minor brings together faculty from departments across the university to provide students with a broad understanding of the forms, functions and history of religion. The minor prepares students for graduate study in religion, seminary, and for a variety of professions in which knowledge of religion is critical, including teaching, law, social work, journalism, public service and the arts. The minor helps students develop critical thinking and communication skills and an understanding of diverse peoples and cultures.

Department: College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism
Description: The Retailing minor is designed for students outside the G. Brint Ryan College of Business who want to gain expertise in retailing operations and strategies. The minor complements a variety of majors including fashion design, merchandising, communication studies, hospitality management, journalism, marketing (non-business major), and visual arts. Students completing the minor will have an understanding of the retail industry including store operations, buying, supply chain issues and marketing.

Department: College of Business
Description: Students in risk management and insurance learn to identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks associated with business operations. They gain an understanding of how insurance works, including different types of coverage, policies, and regulations. They also learn about risk assessment, loss control, and claims management. Graduates with a BBA in risk management and insurance are prepared for careers in various sectors, including insurance companies, brokerage firms, corporate risk management departments, and regulatory agencies. Common job titles include insurance underwriter, claims adjuster, risk analyst, and employee benefits specialist. The curriculum covers topics such as property and liability insurance, life and health insurance, employee benefits, and enterprise risk management. Students develop analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills essential for success in this dynamic field.
Accredidation: The College of Business is accredited by AACSB International.
